analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches and metadata. DistributedInstalledPairServingGrant.swift:668-678 now labels tensor-assistant traffic eligible when the artifact has a public assistant declaration, and uses ClusterPublicModels.current; this is presentation, not demonstrated authorization. ClusterPlacementTensorAssistantSelection.swift's patch (head:46-48, 112-120, 137-149) enables coordinator automatic discovery for declared assistants, supplies their depth/verification arguments and requires exact returned policy equality. Existing manifest/artifact bindings, request-scope checks, kill switch, private-image exclusion, deadlines and bounded probe output remain. ClusterApprovalAttachment.swift changes only comments at head:135-138; unchanged checks bind model/schedule/expiry, artifact or build facts (including resource_policy_sha256 at :26), pairing roster and local rank, then call configuration validation at :139-140 before saving.
No supported regression is established within this scope. Relevant contracts are output integrity/model binding (T-007, T-012, T-027), serving authorization/build qualification (T-052 through T-056), and resource availability (A-018, TB-007). No supplied changes alter encryption, credentials, billing, media handling or T-041 cache controls.
Integration must examine ClusterPublicModels declaration provenance/current overrides, ClusterConfiguration.validate's exact assistant-policy enforcement, callers passing coordinator into readAutomatic, and resource-policy digest/LOAD/runtime verification plumbing. Confirm that declared assistant eligibility cannot replace coordinator placement parity or App Attest serving authorization, and that quotes reserve the same assistant resources actually loaded. Those implementations are outside the supplied scope; their absence is not evidence of a bypass. The canonical index provides selected details, not full definitions of every boundary.
